senses.d: Security, usually a sum of money, exchanged for the release of an arrested person as a guarantee of that person's appearance for trial.
ex: He was granted bail for £20000.

senses.d: Release from imprisonment on payment of such money.
The person providing such payment.
A bucket or scoop used for removing water from a boat etc.
ex: The bail of a canoe […] made of a human skull.

senses.d: A person who bails water out of a boat.
Custody; keeping.
ex: Silly Faunus now within their baile.

senses.d: To secure the release of an arrested person by providing bail.
To release a person under such guarantee.
To hand over personal property to be held temporarily by another as a bailment.

senses.d: To remove (water) from a boat by scooping it out.

senses.d: To remove water from (a boat) by scooping it out.

senses.d: To set free; to deliver; to release.
ex: Ne none there was to reskue her, ne none to baile.

ex: "No one bails on Bennie Milagros. No one, comprende? I'm gonna hold you to that midnight run — "

To confine.
To secure (a cow) by placing its head in a bail for milking.
To keep (a traveller) detained in order to rob them; to corner (a wild animal); loosely, to detain, hold up.
ex: While celebrating our “graduation”, a handsome Scot bailed me up outside a pub and insisted I help him solve the cryptic crossword.
